blocks.html:
There are lots of words and phrases that, in everyday conversation, work well enough. But when you start trying to think carefully, they will fail you. To start thinking clearly, you need something of a philosophical vocabulary, a starting point for thinking about the relationship between your mind, the world, and the reasons that connect you to the world. This reading will help give you just such a vocabulary.

Statements are the middle-men between linguistic minds (like ours) and the world. They aim at describing reality. When a statement successfully linguistically represents the world, that statement is a true statement. When a statement fails to represent the world, that statement is a false statement. Now we come to a very important conclusion. Every statement is either true or false. Every statement also has a contradiction. No statement and its contradiction can both be simultaneously true in the same sense. From those claims together it follows that the following statements are either true or false, and cannot be both true and false:

The Christian God exists. (Or the Christian God does not exist.)

Jesus died for the sins of humanity. (Or Jesus did not die for the sins of humanity.)

There will be a future resurrection of the dead. (Or there will not be a future resurrection of the dead.)

Jesus is not God, but a human prophet. (Or Jesus is not a human prophet, but is God.)

The movements of the stars and planets determine oneÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¾Ã‚Â¢s personality traits. (Or the movements of the stars and planets do not determine oneÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¾Ã‚Â¢s personality traits.)

It is possible to manifest something into reality just by believing it will happen. (Or it is not possible to manifest something into reality just by believing it will happen.)

To give someone a benefit on the basis of their race is wrong. (Or to give someone a benefit on the basis of their race is not wrong.)

Elective abortions are sometimes good acts. (Or elective abortions are never good acts.)

Intentionally killing an innocent human being is never good. (Or intentionally killing an innocent human being is sometimes good.)

A society would be better off with less federal governmental intervention. (Or a society would not be better off with less federal governmental intervention.)

Transgender women are women in the same sense that non-transgender women are women. (Or transgender women are not women in the same sense that non-transgender women are women.)

To have sex with someone with the same reproductive organs is wrong. (Or to have sex with someone with the same reproductive organs is not wrong.)

To have a society where all members are valued equally, it is necessary to have laws in place to give benefits to the less well-off. (Or to have a society where all members are valued equally, it is not necessary to have laws in place to give benefits to the less well-off.)

If a person has lost higher brain functions, but have other biological or brain functions, they are dead. (Or if a person has lost higher brain functions, but have other biological or brain functions, they are not dead.)

To repeat, all of the above statements are either true or false, and cannot be both true and false. Whether they are true or false has nothing to do with what anyone believes about them.
